note: Alert rules for LouNgak Watch. Each rule states its status: SOURCED (thresholds taken from a named authority; still to be confirmed against the original), PLACEHOLDER (an engineering choice, not agronomically verified) or UNVALIDATED (a rule whose agronomic thresholds are placeholders). An alert from a PLACEHOLDER or UNVALIDATED rule is published only as a qualified watch, never as a validated warning.

heavy_rain.source: India Meteorological Department (IMD) terminology for 24-hour rainfall intensity: heavy 64.5-115.5 mm, very heavy 115.6-204.4 mm, extremely heavy 204.5 mm or more (IMD forecast glossary, mausam.imd.gov.in). To be confirmed against the current IMD glossary.
heavy_rain.limitation: IMD's categories describe 24-hour rainfall at a place. Here they are applied to a weather model's daily forecast total for one grid point per zone, not to an IMD forecast or warning. A heavy-rain forecast is not evidence of flooding or crop damage.

crop_health.limitation: NDVI measures vegetation vigour over all clear land in the zone (crops, trees, grass), not cropland alone. A drop can come from harvest, sowing timing, water stress, flooding or land-cover change; it is not a disease or pest diagnosis. October-November is the kharif paddy harvest period in the Manipur valley, so a seasonal drop is expected.

pest_watch.limitation: The pest and disease weather rules are PLACEHOLDERS awaiting agronomist review (satquery/agri/assets/pest_rules.json). Conducive weather is not evidence that a pest or disease is present; only field scouting can show that.
